open up: verb
become available or possible (opportunities)
typical: opportunities open up, open sth up. NOT for: closing.
A whole new world opens up with a microscope.
The agreement opens up new possibilities.
verb
make an area easier to reach or ready for use
typical: open up an area/market. NOT for: closing.
They opened up the region for tourism.
Roads opened up the valley.
verb
start talking more freely about your feelings
typical: open up (to sb). NOT for: hiding feelings.
He finally opened up to me about his fears.
She found it hard to open up.
verb
unlock a building or start business (a shop)
typical: open (sth) up. NOT for: closing.
I open up at eight every morning.
She opened up the shop.
verb
start shooting (open up on sb)
typical: open up (on sb). NOT for: ceasing fire.
The soldiers opened up on the enemy.
The guns opened up.
opt out: typical: opt out (of sth). NOT for: accepting.
You can't just opt out of all responsibility.
He opted out of the job.
decide not to be part of a group or system
typical: opt out (of sth). NOT for: joining.
Britain wants to opt out of the new rules.
She opted out of the scheme.
decide to manage its own money instead of being run by a local authority (a school or hospital in Britain)
typical: a school/hospital opts out. NOT for: staying in the system.
The school voted to opt out of local control.
own up: admit that you have done something wrong
typical: own up (to sth/doing sth). NOT for: denying.
Come on, own up. Who broke it?
No one owned up to breaking the window.
